chunks.title: Antibody-mediated eye disease & allergy
chunks.tldr: Eye is immune-privileged yet often hit: vascular uvea, immune-complex deposition, exposed conjunctiva. 'Antibody-mediated' if e.g. more antibody in eye fluid than serum, plasma cells/Ig/complement or eosinophils at the site. Allergic conjunctivitis (seasonal = pollen; perennial = mites, mould, dander): type I — allergen binds IgE on conjunctival mast cells → histamine/leukotrienes → itch, chemosis. Eosinophils on scraping; skin prick tests; tear/serum IgE. Rx: avoid allergen, cold, lubricants → antihistamine/mast-cell stabiliser → dual agents → short steroid; allergen immunotherapy (sublingual/subcut) for severe/rhinoconjunctivitis.

cards.a: Type I hypersensitivity — allergen cross-links IgE on conjunctival mast cells, releasing histamine and leukotrienes.

chunks.title: AKC vs VKC immunology; joints & HLA
chunks.tldr: VKC: kids, hot dry climate, giant upper tarsal papillae, Trantas dots, shield ulcer (plaque may need removal); Th2-driven, many degranulated eosinophils; mast-cell stabilisers help. AKC: late teens–50s, perennial, eczema, lower papillae, scarring/vascularisation, HSV keratitis, cataract, keratoconus; Th1-driven; often needs steroid; ciclosporin/tacrolimus. Joints: RA → scleritis (immune-complex occlusive vasculitis, RF/anti-CCP), PUK, secondary Sjögren; JIA oligoarticular ANA+ → silent chronic AU; HLA-B27 enthesitis JIA, AS → acute AU with fibrin; reactive arthritis (Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Chlamydia) → conjunctivitis then iridocyclitis. MMP: antibodies to basement membrane hemidesmosome protein → subepithelial bullae, fornix shrinkage, keratinisation → systemic immunosuppression.

cards.q: Which T-helper subset drives VKC vs AKC?
cards.a: VKC: Th2. AKC: Th1 (both have mast cell/IgE components).

chunks.title: Granulomatous & cell-mediated eye disease
chunks.tldr: Type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity: lymphocytes + macrophages; antigens from TB, leprosy, toxo, zoster (skin-test positive), or unknown (sarcoid). Sarcoid: non-caseating granulomas; biopsy (node, skin, lung/BAL); hilar nodes, ↑ACE, anergic tuberculin, gallium. Sympathetic ophthalmia: exposure of hidden uveal antigens after trauma/surgery → bilateral granulomatous uveitis, Dalen-Fuchs, ± vitiligo/poliosis. VKH: melanocyte antigens, pigmented races (Hispanic, Japanese); meningeal prodrome (headache, CSF lymphocytosis, tinnitus, hearing loss) → panuveitis, disc oedema, exudative RD → vitiligo, poliosis, alopecia; FFA pinpoint RPE leaks, US choroidal thickening. GCA, PAN, GPA (C-ANCA), Behçet (immune complexes, HLA-B51). Contact dermatitis (brimonidine, atropine, preservatives — lower lid worse). Phlyctenulosis (TB, staph). SJS/TEN: keratinocyte apoptosis.
chunks.hook: Red, itchy, scaly lower lids after new drops = contact dermatitis (type IV).

cards.q: Fluorescein and ultrasound findings in acute VKH?
cards.a: Multiple pinpoint RPE leaks pooling into serous detachments; diffuse choroidal thickening on B-scan.

cards.q: Why is the lower lid more affected in drop-induced contact dermatitis?
cards.a: Drops pool and run over the lower lid skin.

chunks.title: Corneal graft rejection & immunotherapy
chunks.tldr: Cornea is a relatively privileged allograft — no routine HLA match: PK 1-y survival ≥85%, low-risk 5-y >90%; high-risk (vascularised, inflamed, regraft, young, HSV, prior surgery) ~55% at 5 y. Antigens mainly on endothelium → DALK/EK reduce rejection. Early rejection (2–4 wk) cell-mediated: Khodadoust endothelial rejection line, KPs, oedema; epithelial line; stromal infiltrates; late can be antibody/complement (rings). Rx: intensive topical steroid (hourly) ± systemic/IV steroid, ciclosporin/tacrolimus; endothelial damage often irreversible. High-risk: HLA/ABO matching, pre-op aza/ciclosporin/MMF. Immunotherapy: antimetabolites (aza, MTX, MMF), calcineurin inhibitors, alkylators (cyclophosphamide, chlorambucil); biologics: anti-TNF (adalimumab, infliximab), rituximab (CD20), tocilizumab/sarilumab (IL-6R), secukinumab (IL-17), anakinra (IL-1), daclizumab, interferons; intravitreal MTX.
chunks.hook: RSVP for a rejecting graft: Redness, Sensitivity to light, Vision down, Pain.

cards.q: Which corneal layer carries most graft-rejection antigens?
cards.a: The endothelium (hence endothelial rejection threatens graft survival most).
